Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are extending `@twyne/tools` at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/packages/twyne-tools (a Node >=20 ESM package: `twyne` CLI in src/cli.ts, `twyne-mcp` stdio MCP server in src/mcp.ts, `TwyneClient` in src/client.ts, types in src/types.ts; tests in test/ run with `bun test`; `bun run check` is tsc). Twyne is a writing app. Its model-backed features (room of editors, rewrites, rubric grading, dossier check, dossier interview) are being exposed through the existing personal-access-token integration API `POST /api/integrations/v1`. Another agent is implementing the server side right now. Your job is the client side: TwyneClient methods, CLI commands and MCP tools. These are how evals and external agents drive the app, and the CLI must be scriptable in tests.

READ FIRST: `/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/docs/app-harness.md`. This is the contract: operation names, request fields, response shapes. Implement it exactly. Then read every file in src/ and test/ of the package to match its conventions (parseArgs-based CLI, `CliIo` injection, `textResult`/`toolError` in mcp.ts, zod/v4 input schemas, fake-fetch tests).

WHAT TO BUILD
1. src/types.ts: types for `EditorNote`, `EditorSummary`, `RubricGrade`, `DossierCheckResult`, `InterviewTurnResult` (loose but useful, e.g. `[key: string]: unknown`), and the input shapes of each operation.
2. src/client.ts: `listEditors()`, `conveneRoom(input)`, `askEditor(input)`, `suggestRewrite(input)`, `gradeDraft(input)`, `checkDossier(input)`, `interviewTurn(input)`. Each sends `{ operation, ...fields }` through the existing `request()` and accepts an optional AbortSignal like the existing methods. Pass through only defined fields.
3. src/mcp.ts: add exactly five tools, so the total is 15: `twyne_convene_room`, `twyne_ask_editor`, `twyne_suggest_rewrite`, `twyne_grade_draft`, `twyne_interview_turn` (dossier.check and editors.list stay CLI and client only, which keeps the MCP surface at the existing hard cap of 15). Update `TWYNE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES`. Use input schemas that accept `folioId` OR `draftText` (validate that exactly one is present inside the handler and return a toolError otherwise), `personaId` as `z.enum(["devil","angel","scholar","editor","reader"])`, and describe each editor in the tool description (devil = sceptic who attacks the argument, angel = patron who protects what works, scholar = evidence and sources, editor = line and structure, reader = the target reader; get the real names and roles from /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/src/utils/personas.ts). Descriptions should tell an agent when to use each tool (for example: convene the room for a full read, ask one editor for a follow-up or a reply, suggest_rewrite for a concrete replacement of a passage that appears verbatim in the draft, grade_draft for the rubric). Annotations: these spend model credits and do not modify stored data, so use `readOnlyHint: true, idempotentHint: false, openWorldHint: true`. Return results through the existing `resultOf`/`textResult` so `structuredContent` carries them. For `twyne_convene_room`, return `{ notes }`.
4. src/cli.ts: add commands, keeping the existing style and the HELP text:
   - `twyne editors list [--json]`
   - `twyne room convene (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--editors devil,angel] [--brief FILE] [--locale xx] [--json]`
   - `twyne editor ask PERSONA (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--instruction feedback|elaborate|riff|rewrite-suggestion] [--message TEXT] [--anchor TEXT] [--brief FILE] [--json]`
   - `twyne rewrite PERSONA (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) --original TEXT [--level sentence|paragraph] [--brief FILE] [--json]`
   - `twyne grade (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--brief FILE] [--criteria FILE] [--json]`
   - `twyne dossier check --brief FILE (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--json]`
   - `twyne interview turn --messages FILE [--mode first-run|refine] [--brief FILE] [--starting FILE] [--json]`
   Draft files: `.html`/`.htm` become plain text (strip tags and decode basic entities), and `.md`/`.txt`/anything else is used as-is. `--stdin` reads the draft from stdin (CliIo needs a stdin hook for tests, so add one in the existing injection style). `--brief`/`--criteria`/`--messages` read JSON files. With `--json`, print exactly the operation's `data` as JSON (machine-readable, for tests and evals). Without it, print a compact human summary: notes as `[Editor Name] (type) text` with `> anchor` lines, the grade as a letter plus a per-judge table, a rewrite as replacement plus rationale. Exit code 0 on success, 1 on any error, as the CLI already does.
5. Tests (bun test, fake fetch like the existing tests): client methods send the right operation and body; the MCP tool list is exactly the 15 names (update the existing "exact 10" test to the new list and keep the `<= 15` cap assertion); each new MCP tool round-trips through `InMemoryTransport` with a fake TwyneClient fetch; the folioId/draftText exclusivity check; CLI `--json` output for `room convene --file`, `grade --stdin`, and `editor ask` with `--message`; HTML-file-to-text conversion.
6. README.md: document the new CLI commands and MCP tools. The "exactly 10 focused tools" wording becomes 15, grouped as data tools and room tools. Add a short "Driving Twyne in tests" section: the CLI and MCP server work against any deployment through `TWYNE_API_URL` and `TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, including the in-process local app the repo's evals start (`bun evals/app/local-app.ts --model mock`, see docs/app-harness.md).

Verification: run `bun test` in the package (it is fast) and `bun run check` once at the end, then fix anything they surface. Also run `bun run build` once so dist/ is fresh (the evals may spawn `node dist/mcp.js`).

RULES: Only edit files under packages/twyne-tools/. Other agents are working elsewhere in this same checkout, so do not touch other paths. Do not run git commands that change state (no stash, checkout, reset, commit, add). Do not add new runtime dependencies. Final report: list the files changed, the new tool and command list, test and check output summary lines, and anything in the contract you found ambiguous.
I’ll read the harness contract and package conventions, implement the client, CLI, and MCP additions within `packages/twyne-tools/`, then run the tests, typecheck, and build.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/packages/twyne-tools/README.md
@@
-- `twyne`, a CLI for authentication, folios, critiques, and citations.
-- `twyne-mcp`, a stdio MCP server with exactly 10 focused tools.
+- `twyne`, a CLI for authentication, folios, critiques, citations, and model-backed editorial work.
+- `twyne-mcp`, a stdio MCP server with exactly 15 focused tools.
@@
 `citations.json` may contain one citation object or an array. A title is required. Supplying an existing `id` updates that citation; omitting it creates one.
+
+### The editorial room
+
+```sh
+twyne editors list [--json]
+twyne room convene (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--editors devil,angel] [--brief FILE] [--locale xx] [--json]
+twyne editor ask PERSONA (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--instruction feedback|elaborate|riff|rewrite-suggestion] [--message TEXT] [--anchor TEXT] [--brief FILE] [--json]
+twyne rewrite PERSONA (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) --original TEXT [--level sentence|paragraph] [--brief FILE] [--json]
+twyne grade (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--brief FILE] [--criteria FILE] [--json]
+twyne dossier check --brief FILE (--folio ID | --file FILE | --stdin) [--json]
+twyne interview turn --messages FILE [--mode first-run|refine] [--brief FILE] [--starting FILE] [--json]
+```
+
+Choose exactly one draft source. HTML/HTM files are stripped to plain text with
+basic entities decoded; Markdown, text, and other files are passed through
+unchanged. Stdin is plain text and retains whitespace. With `--folio`, the server
+loads the saved draft and its brief unless you supply a brief explicitly.
+
+The five editors are `devil` (Mlle. Sceptique, argument), `angel` (Sœur
+Encourageante, strengths), `scholar` (Professeur Athenæum, evidence), `editor`
+(M. Le Stylo, line and structure), and `reader` (Le Lecteur, audience fit).
+Convene the room for a full read; ask one editor for a follow-up using `--message`.
+Rewrites require an `--original` passage appearing verbatim in the draft and
+default to `--level sentence`. The room's `--locale` accepts `en`, `fr`, `es`,
+`zh`, `hi`, or `ja`.
+
+`--brief`, `--criteria`, and `--messages` read JSON files. Criteria are an array
+of `{ "label": "Clarity", "description": "Can the reader follow the argument?" }`.
+Messages are an array of `{ "author": "writer" | "interviewer", "text": "..." }`.
+Interviews default to `--mode first-run`; `--brief` supplies `currentBrief`, and
+`--starting` reads manuscript text (with the same HTML conversion as draft files).
+
+Model-backed operations spend model credits and return results without writing
+to the folio. `--json` prints exactly the operation's `data`, including the
+`{ notes }` and `{ note }` envelopes. Without it, commands print compact readable
+summaries. Success exits with code 0; errors go to stderr and exit with code 1.
+
+The same operations are available through `TwyneClient`: `listEditors()`,
+`conveneRoom(input)`, `askEditor(input)`, `suggestRewrite(input)`,
+`gradeDraft(input)`, `checkDossier(input)`, and `interviewTurn(input)`. Each
+accepts an optional final `AbortSignal`. Inputs and results are exported types;
+optional fields are omitted when undefined, while explicit `null` is preserved.
@@
-The tool surface is deliberately small:
+The tool surface has exactly 15 tools, grouped by purpose.
+
+Data tools:
@@
 10. `twyne_upsert_citations`
+
+Room tools:
+
+11. `twyne_convene_room` — full read from all five editors or selected `personaIds`.
+12. `twyne_ask_editor` — feedback, a follow-up, or a conversational reply from one editor.
+13. `twyne_suggest_rewrite` — concrete replacement of a verbatim passage, with rationale.
+14. `twyne_grade_draft` — rubric grade, per-judge scores, and optional custom criteria.
+15. `twyne_interview_turn` — next dossier question or synthesized brief from interview messages.
+
+The first four room tools require exactly one of `folioId` or `draftText`.
+`twyne_suggest_rewrite` also requires `personaId`, `original`, and `level`;
+`twyne_interview_turn` requires `messages` and `mode`. Room tools are read-only,
+non-idempotent model calls that spend credits. `editors.list` and `dossier.check`
+are available through the CLI and client only, keeping the MCP surface at 15.
@@
 Successful tools return the same data as both human-readable JSON text and MCP `structuredContent`. For a quick review loop, call `twyne_get_feedback`; it returns persona notes and replies, the rubric, and suggestions together. For grounded writing, call `twyne_list_citations` before research and `twyne_upsert_citations` after using a source so its provenance remains attached to the folio.
+
+## Driving Twyne in tests
+
+The CLI and MCP server work against any deployment through `TWYNE_API_URL` and
+`TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, including the in-process local app started by the repo's
+evals. From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+bun evals/app/local-app.ts --model mock --port 8788
+# Export TWYNE_API_URL and TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN printed by the local app.
+twyne room convene --file essay.md --json
+printf 'A draft to grade.\n' | twyne grade --stdin --json
+node packages/twyne-tools/dist/mcp.js
+```
+
+Build the package before spawning `dist/mcp.js`. Evals can use any stdio MCP
+client and read `structuredContent`; CLI tests can parse stdout as JSON and
+check the exit code. Embedded CLI tests can call `runCli(args, io)` with
+`stdout`, `stderr`, `env`, and an optional `readStdin: async () => draftText`
+hook. See [the app harness contract](../../docs/app-harness.md) for operation
+fields, response shapes, and model modes.
*** End Patch"));
